Repeated-subject time-course evidence. The Issue 226 repeated-subject fixture experiment uses
the rna layer to assess the declared condition target contrasts treatment with control. (A)
Component PC1 shows individual observations and stored population trajectories; the
standardized condition-by-time interaction is 2.22 [2.18, 2.25]. (B) Component PC2 shows
individual observations and stored population trajectories; the standardized condition-by-time
interaction is 0.08 [-0.08, 0.10]. Thin lines connect repeated observations from each subject;
Bold lines show stored population trajectories from the rank-scale model with subject-specific
random intercepts and time slopes. The analysis unit is complete subject trajectory; the design
is longitudinal; the estimand is condition-by-time interaction on the rank scale; time is
recorded as day; subjects are identified by mouse_id; adjustment uses batch. Facet labels
report stored interaction intervals and resampling recurrence. Raw p-values are retained;
q-values use Holm correction across declared components within each metadata field and evidence
variant. No acceptance threshold is applied. Trajectory evidence is exploratory and does not
establish biological validity.
